dialogues.speaker: Hannelore
dialogues.text: Mr. Lohen, I feel we must talk about the matter of confession...

dialogues.speaker: Lohen
dialogues.text: Hmm? Oh? Have I done something that requires confession? You'll have to forgive me, I can't seem to recall anything.

dialogues.speaker: Hannelore
dialogues.text: Do you remember... Struwell? And the others?

dialogues.speaker: Lohen
dialogues.text: Ah, the three noisy brats. I remember them.

dialogues.speaker: Hannelore
dialogues.text: A few days ago, they came to me in floods of tears, practically begging to confess to some pranks.

dialogues.speaker: Lohen
dialogues.text: Oh? Interesting. What did they do?

dialogues.speaker: Hannelore
dialogues.text: ...Sneak into Granny Marthe's house with the grand plan of smearing cream onto her face.

dialogues.speaker: Hannelore
dialogues.text: But when Moricztill was keeping watch, a gust of wind rang the bell above his head, scaring him so much that he fled immediately.

dialogues.speaker: Hannelore
dialogues.text: Then, just as Max was planning to sneak into the room, another gust of wind knocked over a honey jar by his feet. That woke Granny Marthe up immediately.

dialogues.speaker: Hannelore
dialogues.text: Finally, when Struwell was making his frantic escape, a sudden gust of wind brushed his back. Only when he reached his friends did he find a slip of paper clinging to him...

dialogues.speaker: Lohen
dialogues.text: —Let me guess... was it, "The Anemo Archon is always watching"?

dialogues.speaker: Lohen
dialogues.text: Heh. Isn't it a wonderful trade? The world loses three little troublemakers and gains three devout believers in the Anemo Archon... though I'd give them two days, at most.

dialogues.speaker: Hannelore
dialogues.text: *spluttering* Mr. Lohen! Regardless of your motives, there's a limit to how much you should be terrorizing children. Dragging the Anemo Archon's name into it is equally uncalled for!

dialogues.speaker: Lohen
dialogues.text: Now then... which poor, unfortunate soul should I drop in on next?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What are you up to now?

dialogues.speaker: Lohen
dialogues.text: Ah, perfect timing, Honorary Knight. I was just hoping for a second opinion. Would you mind helping me brainstorm a bit?

dialogues.speaker: Lohen
dialogues.text: Tell me, which of these sounds more like a stress reliever? Roasting Electro Slimes over an open fire, or freezing Hydro Slimes?

dialogues.speaker: Lohen
dialogues.text: I love the sound of an Electro Slime being blown into the air... But there's something so satisfying about the feel of a blade plunging straight through a solid block of ice.

choices.text: Why not start by freezing Hydro slimes...

response.speaker: Lohen
response.text: Oh? Now that is an inspired idea. We really must go and try that together sometime, don't you think?

choices.text: Then roast some Electro Slimes with Pyro?

dialogues.speaker: Lohen
dialogues.text: There. Perfect.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Wait, Lohen? Is that... a report you're writing?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: This is a surprise. Paimon always figured you'd hate paperwork even more than Varka does.

dialogues.speaker: Lohen
dialogues.text: Not at all. This is simply part of a captain's responsibility... even if I'm only the Vice Captain for now.

dialogues.speaker: Lohen
dialogues.text: This report concerns the personnel arrangements for the expeditionary force upon their return. It still needs to be reviewed by Cardinal Seamus, who was in charge of administration during the expedition.

dialogues.speaker: Lohen
dialogues.text: By the way, if you happen to be heading back to Mondstadt, would you mind taking this with you?

response.speaker: Lohen
response.text: Haha, that's precisely why I want to entrust it to you, Honorary Knight.

choices.text: But isn't this file a bit too important for me to just... carry back?

dialogues.speaker: Lohen
dialogues.text: Oh, hello, Honorary Knight!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: ...What exactly are you doing?

dialogues.speaker: Lohen
dialogues.text: Exactly what it looks like: shooting practice! I am the Vice Captain of the Ranged Company, after all.

dialogues.speaker: Lohen
dialogues.text: Personally, I much prefer the thrill of getting up close and personal for a good fight... But it wouldn't do to neglect our bread and butter here at the Ranged Company.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: In that case... what's with the apple?

dialogues.speaker: Lohen
dialogues.text: Oh, it's not me doing the practice, it's those two. Hey! Is that aim steady yet?

dialogues.speaker: Ursula
dialogues.text: M—My... my hands won't stop shaking!

dialogues.speaker: Gunther
dialogues.text: A—And m—my eyes! I can't keep them steady!

response.speaker: Lohen
response.text: Ha! A little pressure is the best motivation, right? Besides, their ammo won't hurt me.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: If that's the case... why are they shaking?

response.speaker: Lohen
response.text: Because if they miss... they'll have to undergo my "special training" afterward. Heh.

dialogues.speaker: Lohen
dialogues.text: Well, look who it is. Eating here as well? I must say, your taste is impeccable. This spot has quite the reputation in Dornman Port.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: The food here...

dialogues.speaker: Lohen
dialogues.text: Mm... These are all common Mondstadt staples, but I'm in the mood to try something different today.

dialogues.speaker: Lohen
dialogues.text: I had a dish called "Lohikeitto" in Nod-Krai. Now that we're back in Mondstadt, I wonder if I'll ever get to treat my taste buds to that again.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: The food here...

dialogues.speaker: Lohen
dialogues.text: Mm... These are all common Mondstadt staples, but I ordered Lohikeitto today.

dialogues.speaker: Lohen
dialogues.text: I certainly never expected a dish I couldn't find any fault with... Hmm, I wonder... Did they hire a new chef?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: The food here...

dialogues.speaker: Lohen
dialogues.text: Last time I was here, I had a Lohikeitto that was — even by my standards — absolutely flawless. I found myself returning frequently afterwards.

dialogues.speaker: Lohen
dialogues.text: But no matter how many times I return, I can never quite find that flavor again... Hah, guess there's a new chef in the kitchen. Again.

dialogues.speaker: Lohen
dialogues.text: Hmm... where should I start...?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What are you doing?

dialogues.speaker: Lohen
dialogues.text: The Knights of Favonius recently received word of a disguised thief in the bazaar. I'm here to bring him into custody.

choices.text: Are you actually handling petty thieves like this?

response.speaker: Lohen
response.text: Haha, it's just been far too peaceful lately. And I honestly have no idea why, but ever since I've been stationed at Dornman Port, even the Treasure Hoarders have been reluctant to show up...

response.speaker: Lohen
response.text: It's rare to find someone so clueless... sorry, so "brave" these days. I really must entertain him properly.

response.speaker: Lohen
response.text: Anyway, Honorary Knight, have you encountered any suspicious individuals here recently?

response.speaker: Lohen
response.text: Hm? Are you implying that he's gone to ground? Now that is interesting.

choices.text: Not even going to let a petty thief off the hook?

dialogues.speaker: Lohen
dialogues.text: We've got knights watching every exit, and I've personally swept the entire perimeter... Could he be hiding somewhere... we wouldn't normally think to look?

dialogues.speaker: Lohen
dialogues.text: Hi, Honorary Knight! What wind blew you in today?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Goodbye...

dialogues.speaker: Lohen
dialogues.text: Classic you, always on the move. Well then, I'll see you when I see you.

dialogues.speaker: Uchida Kotaro
dialogues.text: ...Sir Knight! I swear, it's just a plot point for a novel! It wasn't a "master plan" for a crime or anything.

dialogues.speaker: Lohen
dialogues.text: I understand, Mr. Uchida, I hear you loud and clear. No need to get so worked up. Why don't you have some tea and calm down first?

dialogues.speaker: Lohen
dialogues.text: According to intel from a key informant... your manuscript really doesn't look like a "master plan" for a crime. After all, it would be extremely impractical to pull off.

dialogues.speaker: Uchida Kotaro
dialogues.text: Excuse me!? What do you mean "impractical"!? If you're so brilliant, tell me what's wrong!

dialogues.speaker: Lohen
dialogues.text: Too many conditions, and the steps are far too convoluted. You'd need a poison that fits your exact needs, not to mention a building that matches your specific requirements...

dialogues.speaker: Uchida Kotaro
dialogues.text: Uhhh...

dialogues.speaker: Lohen
dialogues.text: One tiny slip at any stage and the whole thing will be exposed instantly, won't it? Not to mention, the setup is so convoluted that it's a chore just understanding it all.

dialogues.speaker: Uchida Kotaro
dialogues.text: ...Now that you mention it, you do have a point. In that case, how should I improve this?

dialogues.speaker: Lohen
dialogues.text: I suppose I do dabble in medicine from time to time. How about we try a bit of this... and then... a little of that?

dialogues.speaker: Uchida Kotaro
dialogues.text: Oh! Honestly, Sir Knight, this job is beneath you! You're far too brilliant!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: About the owner...

dialogues.speaker: Lohen
dialogues.text: Word has it the owner is from Nod-Krai. From the way she carries herself, I'd say she's no ordinary civilian.

dialogues.speaker: Lohen
dialogues.text: We kept an eye on her for a while. It seems she wants to run an honest restaurant... At least, that's been the case here in Mondstadt.
